newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says 15 firms interested in July utility sale.
newsitem.headline: Peru says 15 firms interested in July utility sale.

text.p: The Peruvian government's July 22 auction of a 60 percent stake in two electricity generating companies has drawn the interest of 15 mainly foreign firms, a privatization official said late Thursday.

The government will announce at the end of June which of the interested firms have qualified to bid for the Egasa and Egesur utilities to go on the auction block as one asset, Felipe Repetto, electricity privatization official, told Reuters.
Sources close to the sale said U.S., Chilean and Argentine firms were among the interested firms.

Egasa, which is based in Peru's second biggest city of Arequipa, 630 miles (1,009 km) south of Lima, has a generating capacity of 218 megawatts (MW), while the capacity of Egesur, which operates 200 miles (320 km) further south in Tacna, is 57 MW.
Following the sale of these two assets, the government plans in August to auction stakes in the electricity distributing firms, Electro Norte and Electro Centro.

Peru began its sweeping program of privatizations in the sector in 1994. The government has received $1.693 billion in direct revenue from the sales and a further $240 million in investment commitments from the buyers.
